groups.text: It is currently 19 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

The U.S. Naval Air Systems Command is developing a new weapon to counter increasing Chinese naval dominance in the Indo-Pacific and Arctic. Called the Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo, or SAA-LT, this small munition weighs about 268 pounds and measures 70 inches. The Navy intends for these torpedoes to be fired from drones launched from aircraft carriers or other ships, though they should also integrate into fighter plane bomb racks. This stealthy design allows the weapon to strike underwater threats without being easily detected. Historically, naval forces relied on Boeing P-8A Poseidon aircraft for anti-submarine operations. By reducing the weapon's size, the U.S. hopes to allow drones and fighter jets to conduct these missions. If successful, this shift could reduce the pressure to build more warships while expanding warfighting capabilities and easing the strain on personnel.

Russian strikes on Ukraine have entered their sixth consecutive night, leaving at least nine people dead and 14 injured overnight. Moscow targeted Kyiv and its wider region, hitting a railway depot in the city, while Russia's defense ministry reported additional strikes on infrastructure in the southern Odesa region. These intensified attacks are disrupting daily life for millions of people, who now face up to a dozen air-raid alerts every day. Meanwhile, Estonian Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur reports that Ukrainian drones have again entered Estonia's airspace. NATO aircraft monitored the situation, and no people or territory were affected. Pevkur says this incident shows the consequences of the war are drawing closer to Estonia. He argues this underscores the need for increased support for Ukraine, specifically through air defense systems, to send a clear message of allied unity to Moscow.

At least twelve people are dead and twenty others injured, including two children, following overnight Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and its surrounding region. Ukrainian officials report that fires broke out across three city districts, while a hit on a depot injured six railway workers from the state company Ukrzaliznytsia. Russia described the operation as a massive strike using high-precision weapons targeting energy and military facilities. These attacks follow a plea from Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Vladimir Putin to end the war during a security summit in Kyrgyzstan. In that same city, Iranian President Massud Peseschkian signaled a willingness to return to diplomacy with the United States. Peseschkian stated that Iran would take immediate action if Washington returns to the obligations agreed upon in a June interim agreement, which had previously failed due to disputes over its implementation.

The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into corporate operations has left many organizations scrambling to balance security with the power of these new tools. This tension is central to recent industry focus on building secure AI strategies and establishing proper governance guardrails. Similarly, enterprises are struggling to identify and manage risks associated with cloud assets in this age of AI, as adoption often outpaces a company's ability to maintain a comprehensive view of its infrastructure. These systemic vulnerabilities contrast with the more targeted threat of digital manipulation seen in Nigeria. A Facebook page called Napa Boy shared a manipulated video claiming that Islamic scholar Ahmad Gumi threatened to turn the country upside down if bandits were harmed. Fact-checkers at Dubawa confirmed the clip was an edited compilation and not a continuous recording, though it still drew thousands of likes and shares before being debunked.

The Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array has released new images of the red supergiant star Betelgeuse, revealing a bubbling and unstable surface. These images, captured in 2023, show large regions of gas moving across the star at varying temperatures. Astronomers identified two particularly hot areas in the northeast and southwest, with one region measuring roughly 530 degrees Celsius hotter than the surrounding gas. One of these hot zones appears to be in the same location as a region observed back in 2015. This suggests the structure has persisted for at least seven years, a finding that contradicts current astronomical models. Betelgeuse remains one of the most studied stars in modern astronomy because its mass is nearly twenty times that of our Sun and it has swelled to almost 800 times the Sun's size.

A jury has reached a verdict in one of the most enduring mysteries in music history. On Monday, August 31, Duane Davis was found guilty of the murder of Tupac Shakur. Davis is a former member of a Los Angeles gang. The conviction comes thirty years after the rapper was killed in 1996. Throughout the trial, the defense insisted that there was no physical evidence to link Davis to the crime. Despite those arguments, the jury decided the evidence was sufficient for a guilty verdict. This ruling brings a legal conclusion to a case that has spanned three decades of speculation and investigation.

More than nine and a half million people had their personal and health information stolen in a data breach at Aesto Health, a healthcare technology company based in Birmingham, Alabama. Hackers targeted the firm's Amazon Web Services infrastructure between December 2nd and 18th of 2025, exfiltrating Social Security numbers, medical records, and financial account details. The breach has impacted at least two dozen healthcare provider clients across several states. While digital security fails in health tech, a different kind of instability is hitting European logistics. Family-owned freight forwarders that survived wars and oil shocks now face an emerging succession crisis as owners struggle to pass businesses to the next generation. This volatility extends to global shipping lanes, where Maersk is tipped to slide from first to fourth in global liner rankings within six years. COSCO and CMA CGM are expanding rapidly; COSCO recently invested nearly three billion dollars in 18 new ships.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain cloudy with temperatures between 19 and 22 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has an all-day event for Haushaltspflege and a meeting with Krebs at six in the evening. Your work calendar has a RAYX Meeting at three in the afternoon.
Mail worth checking: You have a user inquiry from Kleinanzeigen regarding your wooden pallets. Also, Sören Wegener and typ o sent messages via the flipdot Forum about an interview request.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
